2609.08435.title: EvolveScaler: Synthesizing Information-Evolution Contexts via Executable State Machines and Natural-Language Rendering
2609.08435.paper_summary: In persistent interactions, long contexts may encode an evolving process rather than a fixed record: later events can revise or revoke earlier information, changing what remains valid and what conclusions follow. We call this setting information evolution (IE). Solving IE requires identifying valid records, applying updates in order, and reconstructing the query-relevant state from the event history. Existing text-first synthesis pipelines make such data difficult to verify because state transitions and answer logic remain implicit. We introduce EvolveScaler, a code-driven framework that defines information evolution before rendering it as natural language. Human-authored operational specifications define state transitions, record validity, difficulty controls, and executable answer logic; a strong LLM then synthesizes a self-contained simulator from each specification. Executing validated simulators produces natural-language multi-turn event histories, while deterministic replay computes reference answers and atomic checklists. We instantiate EvolveScaler with 117 task prototypes and 159 final-question operators across five difficulty levels spanning approximately 7 to 1,200 events per instance, yielding about 35,100 training examples and 585 validated evaluation instances. On the very_long tier, the strongest model reaches 59.3% avg@5, while six models score below 10%. Training an internal A3B model on 6,000 EvolveScaler examples improves performance over its base checkpoint on all eight independently constructed out-of-distribution benchmarks, with a 5.25-point average gain. These results show that code-driven IE synthesis provides both challenging evaluation and transferable training supervision.
2609.08435.paper_summary_zh: 在持續的互動中，長期的上下文可能編碼了一個不斷演變的過程，而不是一個固定的記錄：後來的事件可以修訂或撤回早期的信息，改變什麼是有效的以及隨之而來的結論。我們稱這種情境為信息演變（IE）。解決IE需要識別有效的記錄，按順序應用更新，並從事件歷史中重建查詢相關的狀態。現有的文本優先合成管道使得這些數據難以驗證，因為狀態轉換和答案邏輯仍然是隱含的。我們引入EvolveScaler，一個以代碼驅動的框架，在將其呈現為自然語言之前定義信息演變。人類撰寫的操作規範定義了狀態轉換、記錄有效性、難度控制和可執行的答案邏輯；一個強大的LLM然後從每個規範合成一個自包含的模擬器。執行經過驗證的模擬器生成自然語言的多輪事件歷史，而確定性重放計算參考答案和原子檢查清單。我們用117個任務原型和159個最終問題操作符在五個難度級別上實現EvolveScaler，涵蓋約7到1,200個事件每個實例，產生約35,100個訓練範例和585個驗證過的評估實例。在very_long級別上，最強的模型達到59.3%的avg@5，而六個模型的得分低於10%。在6,000個EvolveScaler範例上訓練內部A3B模型提高了其在所有八個獨立構建的分佈外基準上的性能，相較於其基準檢查點平均提高了5.25點。這些結果顯示，代碼驅動的IE合成提供了具有挑戰性的評估和可轉移的訓練監督。
